title: Fertiliser and the yield response
summary: Crops turn fertiliser nutrients (mainly nitrogen) into grain with diminishing returns: the yield response curve flattens, so the last kilograms buy little grain and much of them is lost to water and air. Here seen across countries with World Bank data.

concepts.label: Country's cropland
concepts.description: A country's arable land, the unit of comparison.

children.label: Fertiliser use
children.description: Nitrogen, phosphate (P₂O₅) and potash (K₂O) nutrients per hectare of arable land, kg/ha (FAO via World Bank).

children.label: Nitrogen share
children.description: The nitrogen part alone, which drives most of the yield response and of the losses; FAOSTAT's fertiliser-by-nutrient domain has it.

children.label: Cereal yield
children.description: Wheat, rice, maize, barley, oats, rye, millet, sorghum, buckwheat and mixed grains: kg harvested per ha.

children.label: Irrigation
children.description: Share of agricultural land that is irrigated: water decides whether nutrients can be used.

children.label: Climate and growing season
children.description: Temperature, rainfall and season length set the attainable yield (the curve's ceiling); not in this data.

concepts.label: Yield response curve
concepts.description: Yield as a function of the nutrient rate, Y = Y0 + A(1 − e^(−cN)) (Mitscherlich, 1909): every extra unit of a limiting nutrient closes a fixed fraction of the remaining gap to the ceiling.

facts.text: Mitscherlich's law of physiological relations (1909) states that the yield increase per unit of a growth factor is proportional to the shortfall from the maximum yield.
Liebig's law of the minimum: growth is limited by the scarcest resource, not by the total of resources.

children.label: Marginal product
children.description: dY/dN = A c e^(−cN): kg of grain one more kg of fertiliser buys at a given rate.

children.label: Economic optimum rate
children.description: The rate where the marginal product equals the fertiliser-to-grain price ratio; needs prices (FAOSTAT prices, World Bank Pink Sheet).

children.label: Partial factor productivity
children.description: Average kg of grain per kg of fertiliser, Y/N: falls along the curve even where the marginal product is still positive.

children.label: Field trial response
children.description: The agronomic N-response is measured per field and crop in rate trials (e.g. the Broadbalk experiment, Rothamsted); the cross-country curve only mimics it.

concepts.label: Nitrogen surplus and losses
concepts.description: Nitrogen applied but not taken up by the crop: leached as nitrate, emitted as N₂O and ammonia. Grows on the flat part of the curve.

facts.text: Nitrogen use efficiency (crop N output / N input) is about 0.4 worldwide and fell in China as fertiliser use rose (Zhang et al., Nature 2015).

concepts.label: Country trajectories
concepts.description: Fertiliser use and yield year by year for eight countries.
